review.summary: I reviewed only the three supplied files. I found no blocker or major defect in them. Parentheses in the reader SQL are balanced. Only gap rows, and registrations/orders rows with proof fields that match the current revisions, can pass the reader. Covered visits/viewing rows are excluded no matter what their sourceRevision is. When rows are empty the reader still returns unknown_history, and gap rows still produce evidence_gap. The migration runs in one transaction with the stated 5s lock and 30s statement limits. CREATE TRIGGER takes a SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE lock on the audit table, so no concurrent insert can add a covered row between the trigger being created and the version UPDATE. The UPDATE only bumps versions that currently have a covered visits/viewing audit, so supported-only versions are untouched. The ACL check fails closed if any role other than the owner holds a privilege. I have two minor findings. First, the guard catches INSERT only. Changing existing audit rows (status or sourceRevision) is not guarded in the supplied scope, so old revision-comparing readers could trust legacy rows again unless an append-only guard I wasn't given already prevents it. Second, the exclusion of visits/viewing exists only in the SQL predicate. The TypeScript layer and the mocked unit tests would not catch a regression. This review does not show that tests pass, that a Prisma CLI upgrade of a populated database works, or that the full WP work is release-ready.

findings.issue: The fail-closed guard fires only on INSERT. An UPDATE of an existing LiveMetricCoverageAudit row is not checked. Examples: changing a visits/viewing gap to status='covered', or moving a legacy covered row's sourceRevision to the newly bumped version revision.
findings.evidence: The trigger is declared 'BEFORE INSERT ON public."LiveMetricCoverageAudit"' with no UPDATE event. The comment in the migration says old readers/workers are protected because they still compare audit.sourceRevision. That protection only holds while legacy rows cannot be rewritten to match the bumped v.sourceRevision. No append-only/immutability trigger for the audit table appears in the supplied scope.
findings.impact: If any path can update audit rows (an existing worker, carry-forward logic, or an owner/maintenance script), old pre-125 readers that compare sourceRevision could again certify visits/viewing as complete. That would reopen the canonical124 defect for old code during rollout. The new reader is not affected, because it ignores covered visits/viewing whatever the revision.
findings.recommended_fix: Make the guard fire on BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF status, kind, "sourceRevision" and reject when the NEW row is covered visits/viewing. To leave legacy raw rows unedited, either reject every UPDATE of such rows, or allow only updates that leave them non-current. If an audit-table append-only guard already exists, cite it in the migration comment and add a test that relies on it.
findings.required_test: On a disposable synthetic DB after 125: (a) UPDATE a visits gap row to status='covered' → expect 23514 or the existing immutability error; (b) UPDATE a legacy covered visits row's sourceRevision to the current v.sourceRevision → expect rejection; (c) confirm the archived pre-fix reader still does not return complete for that version.

findings.area: WHERE predicate 'a.status='gap' OR (a.kind IN ('registrations','orders') ...)' and the TS ranges("covered") mapping; test file 'rejects oversized audits' case
findings.issue: Visits/viewing positive flags are excluded only inside the SQL text. The TypeScript code passes every returned 'covered' row to assessMetricCoverage without checking the kind. The unit tests mock $queryRaw, so they cannot detect a regression in that predicate. The limit test also feeds 10001 covered visits rows, which the real SQL can no longer return.
findings.evidence: ranges = (status) => rows.filter(row => row.status === status) has no kind gate. Feeding a mocked [covered 1000-3000] row for kind 'visits' would make the reader return coverage complete. No unit test asserts that visits/viewing covered rows are ignored. The only stated proof is the DB regression, which was not supplied.
findings.impact: A future edit to the SQL (for example a parenthesis or OR change, or removing the kind IN clause) could silently re-enable certification of unproven kinds. Mocked unit tests would still pass, and fail-closed safety would depend on running the separate DB regression.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a defense-in-depth gate in TypeScript: for kind 'visits' or 'viewing', treat covered as an empty set (still return null when rows.length is 0, to keep unknown_history). Alternatively, assert that no covered row is returned for those kinds and fail with unavailable if one is. Use registrations, or covered-plus-gap, in the oversized test so the fixture stays realistic.
findings.required_test: Unit tests: a mocked [covered 1000-3000] for 'visits' and for 'viewing' must not return complete. A mocked [covered, gap] for visits must return evidence_gap. Keep the DB regression proving the SQL excludes these rows.
